title: Dual and Tate Weil data
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), fix a coefficient stage $A\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ and let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex on $X$: $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ is perfect over $A_X$ and $\varphi_K:Lg_\gamma ^*K\xrightarrow {\sim }K$, where $g_\gamma$ is the geometric-Frobenius automorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. At $A=\mathcal O_E$ the datum includes a normalized compatible finite-stage system and an isomorphism in the derived category of actual coefficient systems realizing $\varphi_K$, as specified in [def-pur-tate-datum]; at $A=E$ its scalar localization, and at $A=\Qlb$ its common finite-coefficient-stage datum. Let $\varphi_A:Lg_\gamma ^*A_X\xrightarrow {\sim }A_X$ be the canonical Weil structure on the constant coefficient object, and let $\tau_r:Lg_\gamma ^*A_X(r)\xrightarrow {\sim }A_X(r)$ be the canonical Tate datum, on which geometric Frobenius acts by $q^{-r}$ (hence by $q^r$ on $A_X(-r)$). The *contragredient datum* on the coefficient dual is the typed composite

$$
\begin{gathered}
\varphi_{K^\vee}:Lg_\gamma^*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,A_X) \\
\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(Lg_\gamma^*K,Lg_\gamma^*A_X\bigr) \\
\xrightarrow{R\mathcal Hom(\operatorname{id},\varphi_A)}R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(Lg_\gamma^*K,A_X\bigr) \\
\xrightarrow{R\mathcal Hom(\varphi_K^{-1},\operatorname{id})}R\mathcal Hom_X(K,A_X),
\end{gathered}
$$

where the first arrow is $\alpha_{g_\gamma;K,A_X}$ of [lem-pod-geometric-frobenius-internal-hom-comparison], at the chosen coefficient stage. The dual is perfect and lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by [lem-pod-coefficient-dual-perfect]. For $r\in\mathbf Z$ the datum on the twisted dual means the typed composite
$$
 \varphi_{K^\vee(r)}:
 Lg_\gamma^*(K^\vee\otimes_A^L A_X(r))
 \xrightarrow{\ \mu_{g_\gamma;K^\vee,A_X(r)}\ }
 Lg_\gamma^*K^\vee\otimes_A^L Lg_\gamma^*A_X(r)
 \xrightarrow{\ \varphi_{K^\vee}\otimes^L\tau_r\ }
 K^\vee\otimes_A^L A_X(r),
$$
with $\mu$ the all-stage isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]; the abbreviated notation $\varphi_{K^\vee(r)}=\varphi_{K^\vee}\otimes\tau_r$ includes this first arrow.

At $A=\mathcal O_E$ these definitions include the following coherent realization. Use the derived strict reduction functor $\mathcal R_X:D(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}))\to D(\mathsf S_{A_E}(X_{\mathrm{proet}}))$ constructed in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], where $\mathsf S_{A_E}$ is the category of actual systems of $(A_{E,n})_X$-modules. On an object it is represented by the strict system $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X$ from one K-flat representative with flat terms; transitions are $1\otimes(A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n})$. Apply $\mathcal R_X$ to each arrow in the two displayed composites, including the specified input isomorphisms $\varphi_K$, $\varphi_A$, $\tau_r$ and their inverses. In particular retain the actual system isomorphisms
$$
 \mathcal R_X(\varphi_{K^\vee}):\mathcal R_X(Lg_\gamma^*K^\vee)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R_X(K^\vee),\qquad
 \mathcal R_X(\varphi_{K^\vee(r)}):\mathcal R_X(Lg_\gamma^*(K^\vee(r)))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R_X(K^\vee(r)).
$$
Their inverses are $\mathcal R_X(\varphi_{K^\vee}^{-1})$ and $\mathcal R_X(\varphi_{K^\vee(r)}^{-1})$ by functoriality. Evaluation at $n$ gives the finite reduction of the displayed integral composite: the Hom comparison reduces as in [lem-pod-geometric-frobenius-internal-hom-comparison], and the tensor comparison reduces as in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Reduction of completed pullback is identified with finite pullback by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]; together with the balancing isomorphisms and quotient cocycle of $\mathcal R_X$ this identifies the source with the pulled-back normalized reduction system and gives compatibility with successive reductions. Thus the output datum retains an isomorphism in the derived category of actual systems, with its finite reductions, rather than just separate derived-category maps at each level. At $A=E$ take the scalar-localized composite and at $A=\Qlb$ its class over a common finite coefficient field, using the scalar-compatible Hom and tensor comparisons just cited and the strict-data conventions of [def-pur-tate-datum]. For $K=A_X$ with its canonical datum, the coefficient-dual identification $(A_X)^\vee\cong A_X$ carries the contragredient datum to the canonical datum. Explicitly, under $R\mathcal Hom_X(A_X,A_X)\cong A_X$ a section $a$ denotes multiplication by $a$; the displayed composite carries its pullback to multiplication by $\varphi_A(a)$, since the precomposition by $\varphi_A^{-1}$ cancels the change of the unit in the source. This is the canonical unit transport at each stage. The resulting $F$-operators are the iterated global geometric Frobenius operators at the chosen coefficient stage. Here the ordinary and compact-support operators are $R\Gamma(X,\varphi)\circ\tau_K$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)\circ\tau_{c,K}$, with transports of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] and the conventions of [def-pod-conventions]; at finite coefficients their compact-support iterate formula is [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description].
